🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin holds near $83K–$84K as Fed comments ease rate-hike fears ahead of U.S. CPI. Security and regulation dominate elsewhere — Ledger pulls devices across Asia, Seoul blocks 27 exchanges — while Kraken, Interactive Brokers and Strive deepen crypto's TradFi push. 📈 Bitcoin Nears $84K as Fed's Williams Rules Out 2027 Hikes Bitcoin rose about 1.5% to just under $83,900 during Asian hours after New York Fed President John Williams said he sees no need for further rate hikes in 2027, though one more increase this year may still be appropriate. Zcash led the majors with a near 7% jump, while SOL, DOGE and ETH gained 2–2.5%. All eyes now turn to the U.S. September inflation report, which could decide whether BTC retests $85,000. Read full story 🔐 Ledger Pulls Wallets From Shelves in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong Ledger asked resellers and distributors in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia and Hong Kong to suspend sales and remove its hardware wallets from shelves while it investigates tampered devices. The move widens its earlier halt at reseller CryptoBilis after thefts tied to covert implants surfaced on October 9. Ledger says confirmed incidents remain limited to Southeast Asia and that its own systems and direct sales channel have not been compromised. More details 🇰🇷 South Korea Blocks 27 Unregistered Exchange Sites, Including KuCoin and MEXC South Korea's Financial Intelligence Unit disclosed decisions to block domestic access to 27 unregistered crypto exchange websites, including KuCoin and MEXC, extending earlier app-store restrictions. The FIU acknowledged the move could complicate withdrawals for existing users and plans to issue withdrawal guidance through industry group DAXA. Authorities say they will now block unregistered platforms without waiting for confirmed user losses. Full report 🇵🇭 Coins.ph Faces Central Bank Action Over Offshore Gambling Links Coins.ph, the Philippines' largest crypto exchange with over 18 million customers, is reportedly facing punitive action from Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas over alleged dealings with offshore gambling firms — infractions one source says could cost it its license. The exchange controls an estimated 75–80% of local peso-to-stablecoin liquidity. Coins.ph denies knowingly serving gambling operators and says user funds are safe. See details 🏦
